football_evidence.question: Can Michigan get Rutgers off the field on third down?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Rutgers, and its own breakdown accounts for about 2.4 of the 4.4 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Rutgers has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Rutgers’ offense is stopped at or behind the line on 12.7% of its runs, and Michigan’s defense stops 18.2% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
In his last two games (Minnesota and Penn State), Underwood averaged 4.5 yards per attempt, against 8.3 in his four games before that.
Tommy Carr has completed 27 of 41 passes (65.9%) for 237 yards, 5.8 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and 1 interception in three games for Michigan, and has been sacked on 5 of 46 dropbacks.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Rutgers’ offensive line No. 18 nationally and Michigan’s No. 85.
contradicting: When Rutgers has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Rutgers’ offense has allowed a sack on 7.9% of its dropbacks, and Michigan’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Rutgers has the ball (big plays on the ground): Rutgers’ offense turns 7.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and Michigan’s defense gives up explosive gains on 1.6% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Michigan has the ball (big plays on the ground): Michigan’s offense turns 5.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Rutgers’ defense gives up explosive gains on 11.7% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
When Rutgers has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Rutgers’ offense averages 5.4 yards per carry, and Michigan’s defense allows 3.5 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).
quarterbacks: Dylan Lonergan has completed 74 of 127 passes (58.3%) for 1,066 yards, 8.4 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in five games for Rutgers, and has been sacked on 6 of 133 dropbacks.
AJ Surace has completed 40 of 71 passes (56.3%) for 539 yards, 7.6 yards per attempt, 6 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in five games for Rutgers, and has been sacked on 11 of 82 dropbacks.
Bryce Underwood has completed 72 of 126 passes (57.1%) for 924 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in six games for Michigan, and has been sacked on 8 of 134 dropbacks.
Tommy Carr has completed 27 of 41 passes (65.9%) for 237 yards, 5.8 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and 1 interception in three games for Michigan, and has been sacked on 5 of 46 dropbacks.
